correctness.rationale: With Lebesgue first marginal, the predecessor branches of the doubling coordinate have equal conditional weights. The Perron operator satisfies P cos(2π·)=0 and maps cos(4π·) to cos(2π·). The Neumann-series solutions of the first- and second-moment equations therefore give exactly the displayed conditional mean and second moment; subtracting the square of the mean gives the variance. The operator is a contraction and |α|<1, so the solutions are unique in L2. The bundled checker verifies the Fourier coefficients and variance endpoints.

value.rationale: The map is a canonical skew-product example whose attractor dimensions are standard benchmarks. The theorem supplies a different exact benchmark: the full x-dependent first and second conditional moments of the stationary vertical coordinate. It separates deterministic phase-dependent mean structure from residual fiberwise variance and gives exact minimum, maximum, and global consistency values. This is mathematically motivated by invariant-density computation and is not a renaming or arbitrary numerical slice.
